buildings.name: Comcast Technology Center
buildings.massing: Block 18th-19th, Arch-Cuthbert (north side of Arch). Slender rectangular prism ~73 m E-W x ~45 m N-S rising straight from a ~12 m tall glazed lobby; south face has stacked 3-storey 'loft' cutouts (indoor gardens) along the east side. Top occupied floor ~274 m, main roof ~279 m (915 ft); above it a ~60 m frosted-glass 'lantern' box (cross-braced steel behind translucent glass, slightly set back, nearly full plan width) reaching 341.7 m (1,121 ft) architectural top. Glass grades from clear at bottom to frosted white at the lantern.
buildings.notes: Silvery glass curtain wall with stainless-steel diagonal chevron panels; Four Seasons hotel occupies the top 12 floors. Tallest in city.

buildings.name: Comcast Center
buildings.massing: Block 17th-18th, JFK-Arch. Obelisk-like rectangular glass prism ~62 m x ~47 m, flat top at 296.7 m (973 ft) with the uppermost ~2 floors notched on one side so the crown reads as a two-pronged slot. 57 floors. Low 3-4 storey glass winter garden (~35 m) on the plaza at the west (18th St) side; plaza facing JFK.
buildings.notes: Silver-blue reflective glass. No spire.

buildings.name: One Liberty Place
buildings.massing: NW corner of the block 16th-17th, Market-Chestnut (on Market). Square tower ~50 m with chamfered/notched corners, rising over a 5-storey base; four stepped gables near the top (Chrysler-style) converging to a pyramidal crown; gable apex ~275 m, short spire to 288 m (945 ft) architectural; broadcast mast to ~332 m (1,090 ft). 61 floors; observation deck at 269 m.
buildings.notes: Blue reflective glass with alternating silver (aluminium) horizontal bands; crown outlined in light at night.

buildings.name: Two Liberty Place
buildings.massing: SE part of the same block, fronting Chestnut at 16th. Near-twin of One Liberty: square tower with notched corners, stepped gable crown and short spire; 258.5 m (848 ft), 58 floors. Joined to One Liberty by the 2-storey Shops at Liberty Place rotunda (~25 m).
buildings.notes: Blue glass + silver bands; upper floors are Ritz-Carlton-era condos (Two Liberty Residences).

buildings.name: BNY Mellon Center (Nine Penn Center, 1735 Market)
buildings.massing: North side of Market, 17th-18th. Square tower ~52 m with 4-storey base to ~20 m; top floor ~210 m; crowned by an open pyramidal steel-lattice truss (illuminated) rising to 241.4 m (792 ft). 54 floors.
buildings.notes: Light gray/white granite piers with blue-green glass strips; open latticework pyramid crown.

buildings.name: Three Logan Square (Bell Atlantic / Verizon Tower)
buildings.massing: North side of Arch, 17th-18th. Art-Deco-inspired: rectangular shaft ~55 x 40 m with progressive setbacks in the upper third; stepped ziggurat crown to 225.3 m (739 ft); top floor ~200 m. 55 floors.
buildings.notes: Red-orange polished granite with punched windows; the tallest non-glass tower.

buildings.name: FMC Tower at Cira Centre South
buildings.massing: West bank of the Schuylkill at 2929 Walnut (30th/Walnut). Rectangular slab ~60 m x ~38 m on a 3-storey podium; top ~6 floors step back on the west; roof edge slopes up from west to east with a fin-like parapet; 222.5 m (730 ft), 49 floors.
buildings.notes: Blue-gray glass; sky lobby near top (AC Hotel). Just across the river - include.

buildings.name: Evo at Cira Centre South
buildings.massing: SW of FMC at 2930 Chestnut: slab ~80 m x ~22 m, 33 floors, flat roof at 130 m (427 ft). Adjoined on the west by the 11-storey Cira Centre South garage with Cira Green rooftop park (~45 m).
buildings.notes: Dark gray glass with angular vertical metal slots.

buildings.name: Cira Centre
buildings.massing: North of 30th Street Station at 30th & Arch. Crystalline faceted form: ~50 x 40 m plan, narrower at the base and top, angled glass facets, sloped crown; 133.1 m (437 ft), 28 floors, flat roof at ~120 m with a sloping ~13 m parapet fin.
buildings.notes: Silver-blue reflective glass; LED-lit facets at night.

buildings.name: 3025 JFK Boulevard
buildings.massing: Just west of Cira Centre. Rectangular mixed-use tower on a 4-storey podium, flat roof 113 m (371 ft), 28 floors.
buildings.notes: Glass + dark metal; 2023.

buildings.name: Philadelphia City Hall
buildings.massing: Centered on Broad & Market. Base: ~148 m (E-W) x ~143 m (N-S) hollow square around a ~61 m square courtyard, 7 storeys; main cornice ~37 m, mansard roofs to ~46 m; four corner pavilions and four mid-side pavilions rise ~52-55 m with dormered mansards. Tower rises from the center of the north wing (above the north portal, ~39.9530,-75.1636): square ~27 m (90 ft) on a side; masonry stage to ~103 m (337 ft), then metal-clad clock stage (four 8 m clock faces centered ~110 m), tapering cast-iron/steel cupola-dome to ~156 m, then 11.3 m (37 ft) bronze William Penn statue to 167 m (548 ft).
buildings.notes: Gray granite base (lower 2 storeys), white marble above, slate-gray mansards, tower above the masonry is painted iron matched to marble. Statue is bronze (dark). OSM likely has building height but not the tower/statue breakdown; model the base and tower separately.

buildings.name: PSFS Building / Loews Philadelphia Hotel
buildings.massing: SW corner 12th & Market. 5-storey polished-granite base (~25 m) with curved NE corner on Market; above it a T-plan slab: a slender N-S tower leg ~25 m wide x ~80 m long stepping from the Market frontage back toward Ludlow, 36 floors, flat roof at 150 m (492 ft); rooftop carries the 8 m tall red neon 'PSFS' letters on a dark-gray penthouse.
buildings.notes: Tower is gray limestone on Market face and glazed tan/gray brick on the flanks; base charcoal granite (#3A3A3A). First International-Style skyscraper in US.

buildings.name: Centre Square II (west tower, 1500 Market)
buildings.massing: South side of Market, 15th-16th. Two flat-roofed rectangular towers on a shared 3-storey podium with a glass atrium between; west tower 40 floors, 149.4 m (490 ft).

buildings.name: The W and Element Philadelphia (1441 Chestnut)

buildings.name: Arthaus (301-311 S Broad)

Suggested defaults for unlisted Center City fabric: rowhouse blocks south of Walnut 12-15 m, commercial mid-rises along Market/Chestnut/Walnut 30-60 m.

buildings.name: Courtyard Apartments at Riverview Tower (ex-Southwark Plaza)
buildings.massing: Single slender rectangular slab, 26 floors (marketed as 25-story senior high-rise), 331 ft / 100.8 m to roof, flat roof with small mechanical penthouse. 1963 Stonorov & Haws public-housing tower; the two sister towers 100 m to the south/west were imploded 23 Jan 2000 and replaced by 305 low-rise (3-story) rowhouse-style units. Long axis roughly N-S parallel to 4th St.
buildings.notes: Address 1021 S 4th St, block 4th/Washington/5th/Christian. By far the tallest object in the bbox. Original brick was a pale 'sickly yellow'; 2018 renovation added light panels/blue accents. Height and levels confirmed by OSM (height=100.8, levels=26) and PhillyHistory (331 ft).

buildings.name: The Residences at Dockside
buildings.massing: 16-17 story slab built on a pier projecting east into the Delaware from Columbus Blvd at Catharine/Fitzwater; long axis E-W (~120 m), stepped at the river end; 3-4 story parking/podium at the street end. 1995, 242 units. Roof ~55 m (estimate from 16 stories x 3.3 m + podium).
buildings.notes: 717 S Columbus Blvd. Red-brown brick with continuous balconies; ground 'Pier 38-40' sheds adjacent to the south (Shank's Pier 40, 1-story ~10 m).

buildings.name: 1001 South Broad (Broad & Washington, Post Brothers phase 1)
buildings.massing: 15-story block filling the east side of Broad between Carpenter and Washington and running east toward 13th St; 2-story retail podium, long mid-rise slab above, flat roof with amenity deck. 600-630 units; phase 1 substantially complete 2025, phases 2-3 (to 1,487 units) planned east along Washington Ave.
buildings.notes: Height 50 m is an estimate (15 residential floors ~3.2 m + podium); no published figure found. Facade: light gray/white panel with large glazing. OSM still tags part of block as construction.

buildings.name: Sparks Shot Tower
buildings.massing: Tapering round brick shaft, 142 ft (43.3 m) tall, ~30 ft (9 m) diameter at base tapering to ~15 ft (4.6 m) at top, low conical cap. Stands alone in a playground at Front & Carpenter (Shot Tower Recreation Center, 1-story ~6 m).
buildings.notes: 1808; one of the most visible verticals in Queen Village/Pennsport; OSM height 43. Immediately west of the elevated I-95.

buildings.name: Epiphany of Our Lord Church
buildings.massing: Large Gothic brownstone church (~35 x 60 m) at SE corner 11th & Jackson, gabled nave ~22 m ridge, single corner tower to 127 ft (38.7 m) with pyramidal/crenellated top; school and rectory attached along Jackson St.
buildings.notes: 1121 Jackson St; tower height 127 ft from parish/Catholic directory sources. OSM has no height tag.

buildings.name: St. Mary Magdalen de Pazzi Church
buildings.massing: Brick basilica (E.F. Durang, 1891) on Montrose St between 7th and 8th; gabled nave ~20 m, facade tower/campanile rising to 36.9 m (OSM LiDAR height 36.88). Rectory attached at 712 Montrose.
buildings.notes: First Italian national parish in the US (1852); closed 2000 but building stands. Tall element is a single square tower on the street front.

buildings.name: Trinity Lutheran (Evangelical Lutheran Church of the Trinity)
buildings.massing: Stone Gothic church at 18th & Ritner with a tall, slender corner spire to 36.5 m (OSM height); nave ridge ~16 m.
buildings.notes: 2300 S 18th St; congregation closed Oct 2023, building extant. One of the two tallest spires in the lower (south of Snyder) half of the bbox.

buildings.name: Annunciation BVM Church
buildings.massing: Red-brick Gothic church 55 ft (16.8 m) wide x 126 ft (38 m) deep (plus 1904 rear addition), nave ridge ~20 m. Central front tower on 10th St was built 120 ft with a 50 ft spire (1863); the spire and corner pinnacles were removed c.1933 and the tower capped flat, now ~34 m (OSM 34.13).
buildings.notes: SE corner 10th & Dickinson (1501-1511 S 10th). Three Gothic portals under a 16x32 ft traceried window; buttressed side walls with nine tall arched windows. Dimensions from the 2019 Historical Commission nomination.

buildings.name: Bok Building (Edward W. Bok Technical High School)
buildings.massing: Art Deco PWA school (Irwin Catharine, 1936-38) filling the block 8th/9th/Mifflin/Dudley: 8-story main slab (~340,000 sf) with strong vertical piers, two internal light courts (E-plan), a lower 2-3 story limestone wing, and a rooftop bar/terrace (Bok Bar) on the roof.
buildings.notes: 1901 S 9th St. Limestone-trimmed yellow/buff brick. 8 floors per OSM; 34 m is an estimate (no published height). Dominant mass in the Lower Moyamensing rowhouse sea, visible from far south.

buildings.name: Holy Ghost Byzantine Catholic Church
buildings.massing: Brick Byzantine-rite church at 24th & Ritner with onion-domed twin towers to ~30 m (OSM 30.17).
buildings.notes: 2310 S 24th St, just inside the western edge of the bbox (lon -75.1873).

buildings.name: Fleisher Art Memorial (former Church of the Evangelists)
buildings.massing: Romanesque former church (1880s) on Catharine St between 7th and 8th with a square stone tower to ~29 m (OSM 29.26) and attached 4-story art-school buildings (27 m).
buildings.notes: 709-719 Catharine St; OSM lists as unnamed 711 Catharine at 29.26 m. Near the north edge of bbox.

buildings.name: St. Monica Catholic Church
buildings.massing: Stone-fronted twin-towered church at 17th & Ritner; towers to ~28.7 m (right tower carries a clock), gabled nave ~17 m ridge; school/rec center to the west.
buildings.notes: 1700 Ritner St (2422 S 17th). OSM height 28.65.

buildings.name: Sacred Heart of Jesus Church
buildings.massing: 1876-77 Gothic church (Durang) at 3rd & Reed/E. Moyamensing; stone/brick nave, single front tower to ~28 m (OSM 28.34), no tall spire today.
buildings.notes: 1404 S 3rd St; school across Reed St (Sacred Heart School).

buildings.name: St. Edmond Church
buildings.massing: Stone Gothic church at 21st & Mifflin with corner tower to ~28 m (OSM 28.34); nave ridge ~16 m.
buildings.notes: 2130 S 21st St; west edge of the bbox, Girard Estate area.

buildings.name: Russell Tabernacle CME (former church, 516 Wharton St)
buildings.massing: Former 19th-c. church with a square front tower ~28 m (OSM 28.34) on Wharton St at 5th/6th.
buildings.notes: Minor landmark; include as a vertical in Dickinson Narrows.

buildings.name: St. Rita of Cascia (National Shrine)
buildings.massing: Roman Baroque basilica (George Lovatt, 1907-08): frontage 90.8 ft (27.7 m) on the west side of S Broad, 178 ft (54 m) deep to Carlisle St; facade a two-stage triumphal-arch composition (paired Tuscan columns, giant volutes, segmental pediment) topped ~27 m; aisles ~12 m, clerestory/nave roof 24.3 m (OSM), semicircular apse at the rear. No dome or tower.
buildings.notes: 1156-62 S Broad St at Ellsworth. Facade is cream terracotta with light brick; north flank is dark Conshohocken stone at ground level with copper-clad clerestory and apse (verdigris). Rectory adjoins to the south. Facade raised 15 steps above Broad St.

buildings.name: St. Casimir Lithuanian Catholic Church
buildings.massing: Brick church at 324 Wharton St (near 3rd) with front tower ~26 m (OSM 26.21).
buildings.notes: Pennsport; minor vertical.

buildings.name: St. Nicholas of Tolentine Church
buildings.massing: Neoclassical/Italian Renaissance church (Nicholas Serracino, 1916-17) at 9th & Watkins: pedimented facade ~18 m, central copper-clad dome over the crossing plus a copper steeple/cupola; overall ~30-34 m.
buildings.notes: 910 Watkins St. Height is an ESTIMATE (no published figure, no OSM height). Dark stone/brick body; oxidized green copper dome and steeple are the landmark feature. Twin of Sacred Hearts of Jesus & Mary, Manhattan.

buildings.name: St. Thomas Aquinas Church
buildings.massing: Large stone Gothic church (E.F. Durang, 1901-03) at NW corner 17th & Morris, described at construction as 'one of the largest in the city'; gabled nave ~20 m ridge; single corner tower ~30-35 m (no spire).
buildings.notes: 1719 Morris St. Tower height is an ESTIMATE; OSM has no height. School at 1631 S 18th (3 stories).

buildings.name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church
buildings.massing: Brick Romanesque church at SE corner 3rd & Wolf with a front tower/campanile ~25 m (estimate); 3-story school (2331 S 3rd) attached to the south.
buildings.notes: Parish founded 1896; locally designated 2021. Height is an ESTIMATE (nomination PDF is image-only).

buildings.name: St. Paul Catholic Church (Christian St)
buildings.massing: 1843-47 church on the north side of Christian St between 9th and 10th: plain gabled brick/stuccoed classical front ~15 m, low square belfry/cupola to ~22 m (estimate); rectory and former school around a small yard; entry set back from the street.
buildings.notes: 923 Christian St, the Italian Market's parish church; height is an ESTIMATE. Sits 60 m north of the bbox top edge? No - lat 39.9394 is inside.

buildings.name: Gloria Dei (Old Swedes') Church
buildings.massing: Small 1698-1700 brick church (Flemish bond with glazed black headers), steep gabled roof ~12 m, square brick tower (c.1733) at the west end carrying a white wooden belfry and short spire to ~20-24 m (estimate; Rudman planned '80 or 100 feet'). Surrounded by a walled graveyard and 2-3 story brick outbuildings on a 3.7-acre site between Christian St, Columbus Blvd and Washington Ave.
buildings.notes: 929 S Water St; National Historic Site. Lies in the pocket between I-95 and Columbus Blvd. Height is an ESTIMATE.

buildings.name: Washington Avenue Pier (Pier 53) / Land Buoy
buildings.massing: Former immigration-station pier rebuilt 2014 as a park: ~150 m finger pier projecting SE into the river from the foot of Washington Ave, low boardwalk over wetland, with Jody Pinto's 'Land Buoy' at the tip: a 55 ft (16.8 m) galvanized-steel spire/mast with a 16 ft spiral stair and blue light.
buildings.notes: Washington Avenue Green park (39.93218,-75.1415) is the landside lawn; Philadelphia Fire Dept marine unit and small tug piers immediately north (39.9331,-75.1416).

buildings.name: Mummers Museum
buildings.massing: Compact 2-3 story box (1976) at SE corner 2nd St & Washington Ave, roughly 35 x 40 m, flat roof; upper floor windowless gallery.
buildings.notes: 1100 S 2nd St. Tan/yellow brick with bands of blue, green and orange tile (roadsideamerica: 'blue, green and orange-tiled building'); murals on the Washington Ave side. Height estimated.

buildings.name: South Philadelphia High School
buildings.massing: 1956 mid-century school: 4-story rectangular classroom block of light tan brick with continuous galvanized-steel window bands, flat roof, plaza-like front entrance on Broad; occupies the east side of Broad St between Snyder Ave and Jackson St back to 13th St, with gym/auditorium wings and athletic field to the east.
buildings.notes: 2101 S Broad St. Replaced the 1907/1915 Norman Romanesque grey-stone boys'/girls' buildings. Height estimated from 4 stories.

buildings.name: Methodist Hospital (Jefferson Health)
buildings.massing: Hospital campus on the east side of Broad between Wolf and Ritner (to 13th St): 1960s-70s brown-brick blocks plus the 1979 'North Tower', roughly 7-8 stories (~30 m estimate), flat roofs with mechanical penthouses, parking structure on the 13th St side; the 135-ft Victorian tower on Broad was demolished in the 1960s.
buildings.notes: 2301 S Broad St, 204 beds. Story count/height are ESTIMATES (no OSM height, none published).

buildings.name: Constitution Health Plaza (former St. Agnes Medical Center)
buildings.massing: Five-story, four-building 295,000 sf medical complex on the west side of Broad at McKean (1970s, renovated to 2012) with an adjoining 5-level parking garage (1485 McKean) and 1-story powerhouse; 30 ft (9 m) monument sign at Broad & Passyunk.
buildings.notes: 1930 S Broad St. Tan brick; height estimated from 5 stories (~22 m). The original 1879/1920 hospital with its rooftop cross was demolished in the early 1970s.

buildings.name: Lincoln Square
buildings.massing: 9-story apartment block (2018, 322 units) on the SW corner of Broad & Washington, filling the block to 15th St: 2-story retail base (Target, Sprouts at 1000 S Broad) with a 360-space garage, U-shaped residential floors above, flat roof.
buildings.notes: 1000 S Broad St. Mixed brick, dark metal and glass; ~30 m estimated (OSM levels=9).

buildings.name: Marine Club Condos (former Marine Corps Quartermaster Depot)
buildings.massing: 4-story (OSM levels=4) long red-brick loft block on the east side of Broad at Washington/Ellsworth, flat roof, heavy industrial window grid.
buildings.notes: 1100 S Broad; height estimated ~20 m.

buildings.name: Philadelphia HS for the Creative and Performing Arts (Ridgway Library)
buildings.massing: 1878 Greek Revival granite temple-front building set back from the east side of Broad between Carpenter and Christian: central pedimented Doric portico with flanking wings, ~20 m to the ridge; lawn (Ridgway Park) in front.
buildings.notes: 901 S Broad St; on the north edge of the bbox. Height estimated.

buildings.name: South Philadelphia Community Health & Literacy Center (library branch)
buildings.massing: 2016 4-story glass-and-metal civic box on the west side of Broad at Morris/Moore, with a 1-story library wing and plaza.
buildings.notes: 1700 S Broad St; OSM height 18.59.

buildings.name: Ss. Neumann-Goretti High School
buildings.massing: Large 4-5 story tan-brick Catholic high school (1930s-50s) filling the block 10th/Moore/11th/Mifflin, with gym block; flat roofs.
buildings.notes: 1736 S 10th St; OSM height 20.72.

buildings.name: George W. Childs Elementary School
buildings.massing: Representative of the 1900s-1920s 3-4 story public schools that tower over the 2-story rows: masonry block ~60 x 40 m with parapets/towers; OSM height 29.26.
buildings.notes: 1235 S 16th St (17th & Tasker). Similar dominant schools: Delaplaine McDaniel 22nd & Moore (27.4 m), Vare-Washington 5th & Washington (27.4 m), Fell 9th & Oregon (27.7 m), Mastery Thomas 9th & Johnston (27.4 m), Southwark 9th & Mifflin (24.1 m), Universal Vare 24th & Snyder (24.1 m), Kirkbride 7th & Dickinson, Furness 3rd & Mifflin, Key 8th & Wolf, Sharswood 2nd & Wolf, Girard 18th & Snyder (16 m).

buildings.name: Italian Market (South 9th Street Curb Market)
buildings.massing: Linear corridor on 9th St from Fitzwater (39.9400) south to Wharton (39.9337), ~700 m, lon ~-75.1583 to -75.1586. Both sides are continuous 2-3 story brick rowhouse storefronts (OSM LiDAR 10-14 m: Di Bruno 930 S 9th, Claudio 926, Fante's 1004-08, Talluto's 944 at 3 levels, Cannuli 937 at 11.9 m, Molly's 1010 at 11.6 m) with continuous corrugated-metal sidewalk awnings ~3-3.5 m above grade projecting ~2.5-3 m over the sidewalk, curbside produce stands, hanging signs and scales; busiest core between Christian and Washington.

buildings.name: East Passyunk Avenue / Singing Fountain plaza

The Singing Fountain plaza is a triangular island at Passyunk/11th/Tasker (2004) with a ~3 m fountain.

buildings.name: IKEA South Philadelphia
buildings.massing: Two-level big box (~200 x 150 m) at 2206 S Columbus Blvd between Snyder and Oregon, flat roof, entrance tower at the NW corner; surface parking to the west along Columbus; on the former CSX rail yard.

Anchor of Columbus Commons (643,810 sf) with Lowe's (2106 S Columbus, 1 level ~10 m, 39.91969,-75.14353), Best Buy (2300 S Columbus ~9 m, 39.91573,-75.13888), Raymour & Flanigan (2110 S Columbus ~9 m), Five Below/Dollar Tree strip (2250 S Columbus, 39.9171,-75.1399) and a Wawa.

buildings.name: Walmart Supercenter / Pier 70 - Columbus Crossing retail strip
buildings.massing: Cluster of 1-story big boxes (8-11 m) with front parking between Tasker/Pier 70 Blvd and Snyder on the river side of Columbus Blvd: Walmart (1675 S Columbus, 39.92651,-75.14148, ~170 x 110 m), Home Depot (1615 S Columbus, 39.92609,-75.14308), Target (1 Mifflin St / Columbus Crossing, 39.92438,-75.14615), strip of TJ Maxx/Old Navy/Michaels/Ulta at 1851 S Columbus (39.9236,-75.1400), Acme (29 Snyder Ave, 39.92327,-75.14504), storage/pet/mattress boxes at 1924-1946 S Columbus.

buildings.name: Riverview Plaza (Regal/Apple Cinemas 17) and Giant
buildings.massing: 1980s-90s shopping center on two parcels split by Reed St, 1100-1400 S Columbus Blvd (west side): 1-story L-shaped strip (~7 m) with Staples/Pep Boys north of Reed, and the 17-screen two-level multiplex (1400 S Columbus, ~15 m, largely glass front, opened 1991, second floor 1998; IMAX refresh 2026) south of Reed; Giant supermarket (1403 S Columbus, ~9 m) on the east side at 39.92927,-75.14381.

buildings.name: Wharton Piers tower (proposed, 1341 S Columbus Blvd)

buildings.name: Pier 78 / Pier 80 Forest Products Center warehouses

buildings.name: Marconi Plaza / Columbus statue
buildings.massing: Formal park astride Broad St between Oregon Ave and Bigler St; the 1876 Columbus monument (10 ft statue on 12 ft pedestal, 6.7 m total) stands on the east half, Marconi bust on the west.

buildings.name: Naval Square - Biddle Hall (U.S. Naval Asylum)
buildings.massing: OUTSIDE BBOX (~400 m north of lat 39.940). Strickland 1827-33 Greek Revival: 385 ft (117 m) front x 135 ft (41 m) deep, 2.5 stories over a raised granite basement; center block 142 x 135 ft with an octastyle Ionic marble portico (8 columns, 3 ft dia) up 19 steps, domed rear chapel 56 ft square with glazed cupola; 3-story wings with cast-iron verandas on granite piers; hipped standing-seam metal roof with 8 double dormers per wing. Ridge ~16-18 m, cupola ~20-22 m (estimate).

Surrounded by Toll Brothers' 2004-09 Naval Square: 5-story brick townhouse rows 14.6-19.2 m (OSM) around Academy Circle, plus Laning Hall and two Strickland residences. Site bounded by Grays Ferry Ave, Bainbridge St, Schuylkill Ave and Christian St.

buildings.name: Graduate Hospital (Penn Medicine Rittenhouse)
buildings.massing: OUTSIDE BBOX (north of South St). 1970s hospital block at 1800 Lombard (18th to 19th, Lombard to South) ~8-9 stories plus the Tuttleman Center at 1840 South St; height ~35 m is an ESTIMATE.

buildings.name: Walt Whitman Bridge
buildings.massing: OUTSIDE BBOX (PA anchorage/approach at Front St & Packer Ave, lat ~39.908, i.e. ~800 m south of 39.915). Suspension bridge: towers 378 ft (115 m), main span 2,000 ft (610 m), deck 150 ft (46 m) above water, 7 lanes; I-76 approach viaduct runs west along Packer Ave to Broad St and the Schuylkill Expressway.

buildings.name: Stella Maris Church
buildings.massing: OUTSIDE BBOX (~270 m south of 39.915) at SE corner 10th & Bigler: 1930s brick church with rectory (2901 S 10th, 8.8 m) and convent; tower ~25 m (ESTIMATE).
buildings.notes: Listed because requested; omit from the bbox model or include as a fringe mass.

buildings.name: Unnamed 1606 Mifflin St structure (OSM height 33.5 m)

Other unexplained OSM verticals: 1425 Snyder Ave 29.6 m (15th & Snyder), 1221 S Broad 27.7 m and 1233 S Broad 26.2 m (7-8 story loft/commercial buildings on the 1200 block of S Broad), 1300 S 19th 27.4 m (5 levels), 1130 Federal St school 28 m, 2000 S Broad 21.3 m (NW corner Broad & Snyder).

area_notes:
BBOX / COORDINATE NOTES: Local x=east, z=south from 39.945474N 75.144748W; 1 deg lat = 111.0 km, 1 deg lon = 85.3 km here. The bbox top (39.940) is at Fitzwater/Catharine, ~250 m SOUTH of South St, so Graduate Hospital, Naval Square/Biddle Hall and CAPA's neighbors to the north are outside; the bottom (39.915) is Bigler St, just south of Oregon Ave, so Stella Maris and the Walt Whitman approach are outside. Camden NJ waterfront is inside the east edge: Battleship New Jersey museum ship (39.9395,-75.1326; 270 m long, masts ~50 m) and Port of Camden water tower/cranes are prominent across the river.

TYPICAL FABRIC (dominant ~90% of bbox): flat-roofed brick rowhouses. OSM/LiDAR heights: 2-story rows 7.0-9.4 m to parapet (e.g. 1840s Carlisle/Rosewood Sts 7.0-8.8 m; 2300 block S American St 7.9-11.3 m), 3-story rows 10-13.7 m (2100 block S 13th St 8.5-13.7 m; 9th St market rows 10-14 m). Lot widths 14-16 ft (4.3-4.9 m; older Queen Village/Pennsport 16'6''-20'), depths ~40 ft (12 m) with 2-story rear ells; porch-front/'airlite' 1920s rows in Girard Estate and Packer Park (west and south of Broad) are 16-18 ft wide, 2 stories, with front porches or projecting bays. Details: bracketed wood or pressed-metal cornices (many removed, replaced by simple parapets), white marble stoops (2-3 steps) and lintels, aluminum/canvas door and window awnings (striped green-white, burgundy, blue), iron railings, sidewalk cellar doors. Facade palette: red brick #9E4A3A / #A5553F, darker Victorian brick #6F4A3A, Formstone/faux-stone veneer gray-beige #BDB5A4 (common in Pennsport/Whitman/Lower Moyamensing), painted stucco white/cream #E6DED0, and pastel painted brick (mint #BFD8C2, sky #B7CBDD, tan #C9B48C); cornices dark brown/white; roofs silver-coated or black rubber flat. Streets are 26-ft cartways with parking both sides; Broad (113 ft), Washington, Snyder, Oregon, Passyunk, Columbus Blvd are the wide streets.

BROAD STREET (lon ~-75.1690 east curb / -75.1702 west curb, bends slightly): mostly 3-story commercial rows 12-14 m with punctuations: Broad & Washington (Lincoln Square 9 st, 1001 S Broad 15 st, Marine Club 4 st); 1200 block lofts 26-28 m; St. Rita's at Ellsworth; Broad Street Diner (1135 S Broad, 1-story stainless diner); CAPA (Ridgway) at Carpenter; library/health center at Morris (18.6 m); Constitution Health Plaza + garage at McKean/Passyunk with 9 m sign; Citizens Bank 2001 S Broad (17 m) / Walgreens / Snyder Plaza at Snyder; South Philadelphia HS (4 st) Snyder-Jackson; Methodist Hospital Wolf-Ritner (~30 m); Marconi Plaza at Oregon. Broad Street Line subway is below grade (Tasker-Morris, Snyder, Oregon station headhouses only).

ITALIAN MARKET: 9th St Fitzwater-Wharton, with the awning-covered core Christian-Washington; 9th & Washington corner buildings 3 stories; cross-street Christian St has St. Paul's and the Palumbo Rec Center; Capitolo Park (900 Federal) is an open block.

COLUMBUS BLVD / DELAWARE WATERFRONT (lon ~-75.143 to -75.145 for the boulevard, river edge ~-75.139 to -75.136 moving south): from north to south inside bbox: Pier 36-40 sheds and Dockside tower (Catharine-Christian), Gloria Dei pocket, I-95 Park deck, Washington Ave pier/green with fire-boat piers, Sheet Metal Workers hall and vacant Piers 53-57 sites, Riverview Plaza strip + multiplex (Reed), Giant, Wharton Piers tower site (proposed), Pier 60 ruin, Walmart/Home Depot/Target boxes (Tasker-Snyder), Pier 68 park, Pier 70 Blvd, Acme, IKEA/Lowe's/Best Buy (Snyder-Oregon), PhilaPort Piers 78-84 sheds. Elevated I-95 (6-8 lanes, deck ~8-12 m above grade, concrete viaduct/embankment) runs N-S between Front St and Columbus Blvd (lon ~-75.1455 at Washington, ~-75.1440 at Oregon) with the Washington Ave and Oregon Ave interchange ramps; a rooftop water tower (~25 m) stands near Front & Oregon (39.91892,-75.14599). Washington Ave itself is a 100-ft-wide former industrial corridor now filling with 5-7 story apartment blocks (The Howell 2101 Washington 6 st, 2001 Washington, 1520 Washington 7 st proposed) between Broad and Grays Ferry Ave.

buildings.name: Benjamin Franklin Bridge - Philadelphia tower
buildings.massing: Steel suspension-bridge tower, two legs joined by portal bracing (arched top portal + cross struts), ~12 m x 40 m in plan at the base (legs straddle the 39 m-wide deck), rising 117 m (385 ft) above mean river level (DRPA also quotes 380-382 ft). Deck passes through the tower at ~38-40 m above water; suspended deck is 128 ft (39 m) wide. Stands in the river just off the Philadelphia pierhead line at local (620,-888).
buildings.notes: Main span 1,750 ft (533 m) tower-to-tower; side spans 717 ft (218.5 m) tower-to-anchorage; total length 9,650 ft (2,940 m); deck 135 ft (41 m) above water at mid-span (local (888,-822)); two main cables (30 in dia) with vertical suspenders. Bridge axis bearing 102.8 deg (WNW-ESE). Colour is DRPA 'Ben Franklin blue', a light greyish blue. Sources: DRPA, Wikipedia. Camden tower mirrors this one at the entry below.

buildings.name: Benjamin Franklin Bridge - Camden tower
buildings.massing: Identical twin of the Philadelphia tower; 117 m above water, portal-braced steel; local (1148,-765).
buildings.notes: 533 m east-southeast of the Philadelphia tower along bearing 102.8 deg. Camden anchorage 218.5 m further at local (1360,-722) (lat 39.951977, lon -75.128834); Camden approach viaduct continues 2,800 ft (853 m) to about local (2160,-352).

buildings.name: Benjamin Franklin Bridge - Philadelphia anchorage
buildings.massing: Massive granite-faced concrete anchorage block, roughly 120 m long (along the bridge) x 60 m wide, ~30-35 m tall above grade with the deck running over its top; occupies local x 340-460, z -907 to -977 (OSM outline), i.e. between N Front St/I-95 and Columbus Blvd at Race-Vine, NOT at 5th St. The 2,000 ft (610 m) Philadelphia approach viaduct descends westward from here on steel/concrete piers (layer-3 motorway in OSM) to touch down at 5th-6th St & Vine (approx local (-200,-1080)); walkway entrance at 5th & Race.
buildings.notes: Former trolley stations were built inside both anchorages. PATCO tracks (2) ride the outer edges of the deck and dive into tunnels beyond each anchorage. Old OSM: man_made=bridge way 575987106 gives the outline; anchorage-to-anchorage measured 984 m vs published 970 m.

buildings.name: Schmidt's Commons (The Piazza at Schmidt's)
buildings.massing: Three 7-storey bar buildings (Erdy McHenry, 2009) wrapping an 80,000 sq ft (7,400 m2) open plaza centred at local (445,-2350): long bar along N 2nd St (1001 N 2nd, footprint x 391-430, z -2401 to -2283, ~120 m x 20 m), east bar at (475,-2352) (~60 x 30 m) and north wing at (469,-2307). Ground-floor retail (4.5 m) + 6 residential floors, flat roofs, ~24 m; large LED screen on the plaza-facing wall. Liberties Walk (3-4 storey pedestrian retail lane) runs west from the plaza toward American/3rd St at z ~ -2415.
buildings.notes: Exposed grey concrete frames with orange/ochre and charcoal metal panels; 8 buildings in the wider complex, max 7 storeys by design. Bounded by N 2nd St (west), Germantown Ave (south), Hancock St (east).

buildings.name: Piazza Alta (Piazza Terminal)
buildings.massing: Post Brothers / BKV Group, opened 2023: one super-block podium (OSM 'Alta', 13,600 m2 footprint, local x 437-618, z -2581 to -2359, Hancock St to N Front St, Germantown Ave to Wildey St) carrying a 5-storey base with a 12-storey mid-rise (1075 Germantown Ave) and a 16-storey, 180 ft (55 m) tower (1104 N Hancock St); remainder of the podium 5-8 storeys (~18-26 m). Tower placement within the podium is approximate (+-60 m): put the 16-storey tower near the podium centre/west (Hancock) side and the 12-storey on the Germantown Ave side.
buildings.notes: Light-gauge steel construction, light grey/white panel facades with dark window frames, rooftop pool club; 1,144 units; phase 2 (431 units, two more buildings) financed 2024-25. Tallest thing in Northern Liberties proper.

buildings.name: Waterfront Square - The Regatta
buildings.massing: 29-storey residential point/slab tower, 100.23 m architectural (Skyscraper Center), footprint ~975 m2 (about 22 x 45 m) at local (935,-1824); completed 2006. Flat roof with mechanical bulkhead.
buildings.notes: Tallest of the three Waterfront Square towers at 901 N Penn St (gated 9.5-acre riverfront site, WRT architects). Buff precast/brick-toned panels with continuous blue-green glass balcony bands.

buildings.name: Waterfront Square - The Peninsula
buildings.massing: 26-storey tower (OSM building:levels=26), footprint ~1,000 m2 at local (870,-1747), on the river pier south-east of the Regatta. Height estimated at 3.45 m/floor = ~90 m (no published figure).
buildings.notes: Completed 2006. Same buff/glass-balcony vocabulary as the Regatta.

buildings.name: Waterfront Square - The Reef
buildings.massing: 22-storey tower (OSM levels=22), footprint ~1,450 m2 at local (823,-1799), west of the other two, completed 2009. Height estimated ~76 m.

buildings.name: 200 Spring Garden Street
buildings.massing: 13-storey mixed-use slab (Handel Architects, completed 2024), 149 ft (45.4 m) to main roof, 177 ft (54 m) to bulkhead; north side of Spring Garden between N 2nd and N 3rd, local ~(200,-1775).

buildings.name: Rivers Casino Philadelphia (ex-SugarHouse)
buildings.massing: Sprawling 1-2 storey casino hall, ~135 m x 150 m irregular footprint (OSM x 993-1128, z -1966 to -2112) with angled 'prow' corners, parapet ~12-15 m; 2016 expansion added a taller event-center box (~18-20 m) on the north side and a 7-storey, 600,000 sq ft parking garage (~22 m) at local (1178,-2102) (x 1113-1244, z -2039 to -2166). Surface lots along Delaware Ave west of the hall. Entrance canopy and slot-machine pylon sign on the Delaware Ave side.

buildings.name: The Fillmore Philadelphia (Ajax Metal Company plant)
buildings.massing: Low industrial complex of seven sections (1907-1951), mostly 1-2 storey brick and reinforced-concrete sheds with sawtooth/monitor roofs, ~12-15 m max, bounded by Frankford Ave (west), Allen St (north), Richmond St (east) and N Delaware Ave (south); 2-storey Italianate brick office at 46 Richmond St. Rooftop 'FILLMORE' signage.

buildings.name: Delaware Generating Station / The Battery (PECO Delaware Station)
buildings.massing: John T. Windrim 1917-23 neoclassical power station at 1325 Beach St: giant brick turbine/boiler hall ~145 m x 100 m (OSM footprint x 1449-1593, z -2315 to -2463), roughly 5 tall storeys / ~35-40 m to the parapet with arched windows and pilasters; eight 167 ft (51 m) brick/steel stacks in two rows on the boiler house (OSM chimney cluster centred (1527,-2364)); a lower 1950s annex with four more stacks at (1676,-2504). Sits directly south of Penn Treaty Park on the river.

buildings.massing: 7-acre (2.8 ha) riverfront lawn at E Columbia Ave & Beach St, roughly 200 m of shoreline; open grass with mature trees, Penn monument/obelisk near the centre, gravel paths, no buildings. Local centre ~(1386,-2645).

buildings.name: Immaculate Conception R.C. Church (Northern Liberties)
buildings.massing: Edwin F. Durang 1870 Italian-Romanesque brick church at the SW corner of Allen St & N Front St (1032 N Front): gable-front nave 62 ft wide on Canal/Allen x 130 ft deep along Front St (19 x 40 m), nave ridge ~20 m; at the REAR (south end) a square four-storey brick tower that rises only slightly above the ridge (~25 m, OSM 24.99). buildings.name: St. Augustine Church

Published height not found - model ~40-45 m (estimate).

buildings.name: Market-Frankford Line elevated (Frankford El) - Front St / Kensington Ave

Model top-of-rail ~7 m above street, underside ~4.6-5 m clear, structure depth ~1.5-2 m, spans 9.6-22 m (31.5-73.5 ft). Stations (Girard, Berks, York-Dauphin, rebuilt 2000s) are side-platform structures ~8 m above street with steel/glass canopies to ~12 m, straddling the intersections. BEN FRANKLIN BRIDGE GEOMETRY (OSM outline way 575987106 + DRPA): Philadelphia anchorage centre (400,-940) [lat 39.95394, lon -75.140068], Philadelphia tower (620,-888), mid-span (888,-822), Camden tower (1148,-765), Camden anchorage (1360,-722). Axis bearing 102.8 deg. Philadelphia approach viaduct (2,000 ft) runs from the anchorage west-northwest over Columbus Blvd, I-95 and N Front St, touching down near 5th/6th & Vine at about (-200,-1080); Camden approach 2,800 ft to about (2160,-352). Deck 39 m wide, 41 m above water at mid-span, ~38 m at the towers, ~33 m over the anchorages; towers 117 m above water; side spans 218.5 m, main span 533 m. Two main cables; PATCO tracks at the deck's outer edges; walkway on the south side. St. Augustine's tower stands ~150 m from the Philadelphia approach. Note the land near the river is only ~3-6 m above river level.

MARKET-FRANKFORD EL: emerges from the subway north of Fairmount Ave at ~(420,-1800) (Spring Garden station itself is underground at (374,-1671)); runs along the east side of N Front St / I-95 edge to Poplar (550,-2068), then centred over Front St (bearing 11 deg) past Girard (728,-2603), Berks (957,-3671), York-Dauphin (1079,-4413), turning at Front & Kensington Ave (1126,-4560) onto Kensington Ave (bearing 55 deg). Double-column steel bents at curb lines, ~10 m deck, rail ~7 m above street (estimate), painted dark SEPTA blue; stations sit above the intersections with side platforms ~8 m up and canopies to ~12 m. Under the El, Front St buildings are 2-3 storey brick rows; several new 6-7 storey apartment blocks have gone up against it (1440 N Front, 7 st).

OTHER SPIRES/LANDMARKS NOT LISTED AS ENTRIES: St. Augustine, St. Peter the Apostle, St. Michael's, Immaculate Conception, First Presbyterian dome, Holy Name campanile are entries above. Visitation BVM (Kensington & Lehigh, green copper spires) lies just north of the bbox (39.9895). St. Laurentius' twin spires are gone (2022). Beacon Presbyterian (Cumberland & Coral, local (1839,-3771)) and Atonement Lutheran (1542 E Montgomery) are smaller brick churches with modest towers (~20-25 m). Summerfield Siloam UMC (2223 E Dauphin). Chimney nodes in OSM: one at (513,-1562) near 500 N Columbus; eight on the PECO boiler house; four on its annex; one at (1466,-4080) in East Kensington.

PIAZZA / NOLIBS BLOCK STRUCTURE: Germantown Ave cuts diagonally NW-SE through the Piazza area; Hancock St (x~455-465), N 2nd St (x~390-420), N Front St (x~640-660 at Allen St). Liberties Walk runs E-W at z~-2415 from (460,-2423) to (332,-2422).

ROWHOUSE TYPOLOGY vs SOCIETY HILL: Society Hill = 3-3.5 storey Georgian/Federal brick townhouses (1760-1830) on 18-24 ft lots, Flemish bond, gable or shed roofs with dormers, brick cornices, marble steps, ~10-11 m to cornice, 12-13 m to ridge, plus 1960s Bacon-era modern rows. Northern Liberties = older (1820-1870) 2.5-3 storey Federal/Greek Revival brick rows on 14-18 ft lots with flat brick cornices (~9-10 m), Victorian 3-storey with bracketed wood cornices (~11 m), many wood-frame survivors, and very heavy 2005-2025 infill: 3-4 storey flat-roofed modern boxes in metal panel/stucco/fibre-cement with pilot houses and roof decks (11-14 m); lots of whole-block new construction. Fishtown = predominantly 2-storey workers' brick rows (1850-1910) on very narrow 14-16 ft lots (some 12 ft) with tiny rear yards, flat or low-pitched roofs, corbelled-brick or small wood bracketed cornices, ~7-7.5 m to cornice; frequent formstone/vinyl/stucco over brick, painted brick, a handful of 1830s wooden houses (e.g. 241-43 E Wildey); 3-storey only on the commercial corridors (Frankford, Girard, E Columbia) and as 2010s infill (3-storey + roof deck, 11-12 m). Porch-front rows (full-width front porches, 2-storey, 16 ft) are NOT typical of Fishtown/NoLibs - they appear only sporadically north of Lehigh and in Harrowgate/Juniata; in this bbox the front is a flat brick facade directly on the sidewalk with 2-3 marble/concrete steps. Kensington west of Front St (Olde/West Kensington) = same 2-storey brick rows interspersed with 3-5 storey mills, vacant lots and new 3-4 storey infill; streets narrower (30-40 ft) with tiny 'courts'. Typical block: 2-storey Fishtown rows 7 m, 3-storey NoLibs rows 10 m, corridor mixed-use 10-12 m, new infill 11-14 m.
